# What your pages did

The person's dashboard shows what happened on their published pages. These are
the same reads, for you. Use the token from
the `mindblown` skill, and take `GAME_ID` from
`GET /me/games`. You can read only the person's own pages.

With the mindblown tools connected, `get_page_errors` and `get_page_stats`
answer the same JSON. They take the `page_id` instead of `GAME_ID`, and
`version` instead of `?sha=`.

## What broke for the people who opened it

Every published page reports the errors its visitors hit. Read them to find
what to fix:

```bash
curl https://api.mindblown.ai/me/games/GAME_ID/errors \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

`GAME_ID` is the `game_id` of a row from `/me/games`. You can read only your
own pages. Any other id answers `404`.

```json
{
  "sha": "063af65dfb1ce6d5",
  "data": [
    { "sha": "063af65dfb1ce6d5", "message": "Uncaught TypeError: Failed to fetch",
      "source": "https://your-page.mindblown.ai/", "line": 661, "col": 12,
      "devices": "Windows Chrome, iOS Safari", "visits": 8, "errors": 8,
      "first_at": "2026-10-15T09:12:00Z", "last_at": "2026-10-21T18:40:00Z", "ours": false },
    { "sha": "063af65dfb1ce6d5", "message": "failed to load",
      "source": "https://connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js",
      "visits": 36, "errors": 68, "first_at": "2026-10-14T21:30:00Z",
      "last_at": "2026-10-21T19:02:00Z", "ours": true }
  ],
  "elsewhere": [
    { "sha": "9c1e2a7700b4f310", "rows": 3, "errors": 11, "last_at": "2026-10-14T20:58:00Z" }
  ]
}
```

What a row is:

- One error message from one file, on one version of the page. `sha` is that
  version, as in `/versions`.
- `visits` is how many different visits saw it. `errors` is how many times it
  was reported. A loop that throws many times in one visit has a large
  `errors` and a small `visits`.
- `line` and `col` are where in `source` it was thrown, when the browser said.
  `devices` is the system and browser of those visits, such as `iOS Safari`.
- A visit reports only its **first** error. A later error in the same visit is
  not recorded, so fix the top rows first and read again after you publish.
- `message` and `source` are cut to 120 characters, and `source` has no query
  string.
- `verdict` is `fixed` or `returned` when a later version showed whether a fix
  worked. Most rows have none.

**`ours: true` is not your page's error.** It is a script, sign-in or image
that mindblown puts on the page, such as our analytics tags, which a
visitor's ad blocker refuses, or a profile picture. Do not try to fix it. Do
not tell the person their page has it. Those rows come after the page's own.

The default is the live version. Ask for another with `?sha=VERSION`. An
empty `data` means the live version has no recorded errors. It does not mean
the page is clean: `elsewhere` names the other versions that have errors,
newest first. One row seen in one visit is often that visitor's browser, not
the page. The rows are updated about every 10 minutes.

## How the pages are doing

The person's dashboard reads these numbers. You can read the same ones with
the same token.

```bash
curl "https://api.mindblown.ai/me/insights?days=30&game_id=GAME_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

- The window is the last `days` days (default 30), or `from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD`.
  Both are UTC, both days included, and a window is at most 366 days.
- Without `game_id` you get every page together, and `pages` gives each
  page's own `plays`, `visitors`, `median_seconds` and `error_browsers`.
- With `game_id` you get one page. These blocks are present only then:
  `changes` (each day the page was published, with the week before and the
  week after), `events` and `signals`
  (every event name the page sent, by day), and `split` (a test of two
  versions).

What the main fields mean:

- `days` is one row a day: `plays`, `loads`, `visitors`, `median_seconds`.
- `plays` is a browser session that started the page, not a person. `visitors`
  is browser-days: one browser on two days counts twice.
- `left` and `stayed` are the visits that reported their time and those that
  stayed ten seconds or more. `stays` is that time as a histogram.
- `runs` counts `game_start` and `game_end`, and is absent when the page never
  sent them. See [Say when a run starts and ends](#say-when-a-run-starts-and-ends).
- `returns` is how many came back after 1, 7 and 30 days. `came_back` is the
  visitors who had been on the page on an earlier day.
- `arrived` is where plays came from: the page's own link or the app, the `?s=`
  tags on links the person posted, device class, time zone and country.
- `errors` is a count over the window and its five most frequent errors. For
  what to fix, read [What broke](#what-broke-for-the-people-who-opened-it) above, which marks ours apart.
- `yours` is the person's own signed-in plays. Every other count leaves them
  out.

A block that is absent was not measured in that window. It is not zero.

The totals over all pages (how many pages, `plays_received`, and `plays_made`,
the plays the person made on other pages), and the round numbers the pages
crossed:

```bash
curl https://api.mindblown.ai/me/stats -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
curl "https://api.mindblown.ai/me/milestones?game_id=GAME_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

A `game_id` that is not the person's answers empty numbers, not an error. You
see only their own pages.

## Watch how people used it

A page can record some of its visitors, so the person can see how it is used.
Recording is off on every page until the person turns it on and picks how many
visitors a day to record. A free plan records at most 3 a day on a page; a paid
plan records up to 100. The recordings are spread across the day. A visitor
who refused optional cookies is never recorded. Names and what people typed are
masked before a recording leaves the visitor's browser.

Ask the person before you turn recording on, and say the number. Turn it on
with a number, or off with 0:

```bash
curl -X PUT https://api.mindblown.ai/me/games/GAME_ID/recordings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"per_day": 3}'
```

```json
{ "per_day": 3, "max": 3 }
```

`max` is the most their plan allows. A number above it answers `403` with the
code `RECORDINGS_LIMIT`, and nothing changes. When they want more than a free
plan allows, tell them a paid plan records up to 100 a day, and that they
choose a plan at <https://mindblown.ai/pricing>. `GET` on the same address answers
the page's current choice.

The recordings of one page, newest first:

```bash
curl https://api.mindblown.ai/games/GAME_ID/replays \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

```json
[
  { "id": "8632e36f-b697-4e55-baeb-1fc95bb18692", "started_at": "2026-10-25T15:21:56Z",
    "device": "desktop", "chunks": 19, "bytes": 748121 }
]
```

A page with no recordings answers `[]`. Any page that is not the person's
answers `404`. A row with `"chunks": 0` has nothing to read yet.

Each recording is `chunks` files, read in order from `0`:

```bash
curl https://api.mindblown.ai/games/GAME_ID/replays/REC_ID/chunks/0 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | gunzip
```

A chunk is gzip of a JSON array of [rrweb](https://github.com/rrweb-io/rrweb)
events, about five seconds each. Join the arrays for the whole recording, which
lasts five minutes at most. Every event has a `type` and a `timestamp` in
milliseconds:

| `type` | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `4` | the viewport: `data.width`, `data.height` |
| `2` | the whole page at that moment, as a tree in `data.node` |
| `3` | a change, named by `data.source` below |

| `data.source` | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | the page's elements and text |
| `1`, `6` | the mouse or a finger moved: `data.positions` |
| `2` | a click or a touch: `data.type`, `data.x`, `data.y` |
| `3` | a scroll |
| `5` | a form field: its value is masked |
| `9` | a canvas frame, about two a second at half size |

A canvas frame names its canvas by `data.id`, the node id from the tree. Its
picture is a WebP image, base64 in the `base64` field of its `drawImage`
command. Decode a few and look at them: on most pages the canvas is all there
is to see. Key presses are not recorded, so a page played from the keyboard
shows its effects and not the keys.
